sources.locator: "Scramble for Africa", revision 1373841219, § lead and § Berlin Conference (1884–1885)

explanation: The period’s own article opens on the conference: “The 1884–1885 Berlin Conference regulated European colonisation and trade in Africa, and is seen as emblematic of the ‘scramble’.” And in its own section: “the diplomats in Berlin laid down the rules of competition by which the great powers were to be guided in seeking colonies … The Berlin Conference transformed Africa’s colonization from informal economic penetration to systematic political control through its ‘effective occupation’ principle.” The type is `enabled` and not `caused`, because the same article says the scramble was already under way when the conference met — “The occupation of Egypt and the acquisition of the Congo were the first major moves in what came to be a precipitous scramble for African territory” — so what Berlin supplied was the rule under which it ran, not its beginning.
